A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MCP-SafetyBench and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The additional reference page in v2 shifts appendix pagination without creating comparison gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs, safety-prompt experiments, and appendix analyses of server counts, attacker budgets, agent strategies, and clean versus attacked conditions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices B–E, including model performance, mitigation experiments, and ablations.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, attack injection, execution-based evaluation, and the safety prompt remain unchanged. Model unlearning appears only as proposed future work in Section 5, not as an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 245 cases across five domains and 20 attack types, including the same clean, decoy-manifest, and multi-server scenarios. Clarifying Function Overlapping terminology does not document a changed test set.

E2.justification: The same 13 LLMs participate in the reported evaluations. Safety-prompt comparisons and the Plan-and-Execute versus ReAct comparison are also unchanged; newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains temperature 1.0, a 2048-token output limit, a 60-second timeout, and 20 ReAct iterations. Evaluation metrics, controls, and the protocols for Appendix D experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same attack-type analyses, safety-prompt tests, server-count and attacker-budget sweeps, decoy-manifest evaluation, agent-strategy comparison, and clean-condition/refusal analyses. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify three repetitions per task and retain the same SD, SE, confidence-interval, significance-test, and effect-size reporting. Appendix B's uncertainty tables and statistical procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and detailed experimental findings remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains overall ASRs of 29.80% for Qwen3-235B and 48.16% for o4-mini. Revised headline summaries emphasize findings already reported in v1.

T1.justification: The task-tuple formalization and dual-outcome evaluation definitions in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds proofs or theoretical derivations; the taxonomy terminology edits do not introduce new mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace claims of escalating vulnerability with growing task horizons and server interactions with all-model vulnerability and a safety–utility trade-off. The introduction emphasizes attack-type variability and host-side vulnerability. The benchmark and taxonomy contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 5 introduces model unlearning as a possible mechanism for eradicating malicious attack patterns and condenses earlier defense proposals, omitting explicit risk-tiered responses. This changes proposed future remedies; existing result interpretations and Appendix E's safe-refusal discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The benchmark repository link, code/data-release statement, construction details, runtime settings, and complete safety prompt remain unchanged. v2 adds no implementation instructions, hardware information, or new resource-access provisions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al. (2025) on MCP security and Shao et al. and Zhai et al. (2026) on unlearning. It expands discussion of Jing et al.'s attack taxonomy and revises MCPSecBench's positioning. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, related work, conclusion, and taxonomy terminology. v2 also adds acknowledgements and updates an affiliation and publication headers. The main section organization and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and the table inventory are retained. Table 2 has a revised definition cell and slight resizing; front-matter formatting and headers change. Acknowledgements and bibliography reflow shift the appendices without reorganizing their displays.

improvement.justification: v2 better aligns its headline findings with the evidence: it replaces broad escalation claims with the established vulnerability and safety–utility findings. This avoids generalizing beyond the narrow server-count study in Table 11 and nonmonotonic iteration results in Table 13. Related-work and terminology clarifications add modest precision. The unlearning suggestion remains untested, and empirical and reproducibility support are unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
